decisions: The filed hypotheses were both overturned by the round-6 refuter, and the refuter's own diagnosis is half right. It said guardCalls's output-active branch re-promotes a preserved range back to killedbycall, quoting the calleepreserves module header. The CODE does not: `if !preserved && fc.is_output_active()` skips that branch entirely (heritage.rs, added in the same commit as the pass, #434). The prose in the module header and in the phases.toml summary was stale; both are corrected here.

The two real blockers were measured, not argued. (1) The callee-body probe declared itself INCOMPLETE on __security_check_cookie: its failure path tail-jumps into a `mov ecx,2; int 0x29` stub, and SLEIGH lifts INT imm8 to a CALLIND. (2) calleepreserves's positive-evidence gate (body_departs_from_convention) requires a write to a register the model marks <unaffected>; the checker writes only RCX and the flags, which win64 already lets it clobber.

The evidence gate was designed against wrongness, not against no-op. The first shape (complete probe + any write outside the stack pointer) moved 22 stage assertions and produced catastrophically wrong C -- `set_qlen` lost `if (v1 < 0) return 0xffffffff;` and every call result in it -- because the ghdec-* fixtures stub out-of-chunk callees as `c3` / `endbr64; ret`, whose only processor writes are the stack pointer and the program counter. Requiring a write to a register the convention itself names (an argument register, or one its <unaffected>/<killedbycall> lists mention) plus more than one decoded instruction takes the stage corpus back to PARITY OK.

The second tightening came from the same measurement: restricting the rule to a callee that writes NO part of the return storage. Without it, a SysV callee that writes RAX and not RDX had RDX narrowed too, which moved the kuna-rustabi negative control.

The acceptance probe was re-cut onto a fixture the repo owns. `pe_cookiecheck_x86_64.exe` (1.5 KB, generator `pe_cookiecheck_x86_64.py`, built on `crtmain_x86_64.py`'s CRT startup so entrymainproto gives main a prototype) reproduces the witness symptom verbatim: `return sub_140001080(v1);` with the option off, `sub_140001080(...); return 0;` by default.

Instance 2 (69d6e9ba, the void wipe helper) was not separately confirmed: its binary `almost` is in the sweep and 3 of its 398 functions change, but the tester named the helper themselves and the address is not recorded in the need.
